definitionAnnotations.name: body
definitionAnnotations.text:
Entering `cpu_state_trap` MUST stop the machine permanently: the state is
absorbing, `trap` is asserted and stays asserted, and **the only exit is reset**
([[FSM-TRAP-001]]).

```text ndf:normative
what stops                     what does not
the CPU state machine          the two counters keep counting -- count_cycle
                               is assigned unconditionally (:1433, CNT-001)
instruction fetch              the timer keeps counting down, and can still
                               raise a pending bit that nothing will service
                               (:1442-1443, IRQ-TIMER-001)
the memory interface, once     eoi holds whatever it held
any outstanding transfer       (IRQ-EOI-001)
completes (MEM-FSM-001)
```

So a trapped core is **not** a quiescent core, and a testbench that waits for
activity to cease will wait for ever. What it must watch is the `trap` output,
which is the only signal that says the machine has stopped
([[VER-TRAP-001]]).

An implementation MUST NOT provide a return path. There is no `mepc`, no
`mcause`, no vector, and nothing reads `reg_pc` after the trap
([[CHR-NG-002]]).

definitionAnnotations.name: body
definitionAnnotations.text:
With `CATCH_MISALIGN`, the core MUST check two alignments after the state `case`
([[FSM-POST-001]]) and escalate per [[TRAP-CAUSE-001]] on interrupt 2:

```text ndf:normative
check                                              guard                 line
a word data access with reg_op1[1:0] != 0          CATCH_MISALIGN &&     1922-1929
a halfword data access with reg_op1[0] != 0        resetn &&             1930-1937
                                                   (mem_do_rdata ||
                                                    mem_do_wdata)
an instruction fetch with reg_pc[0] != 0, or       CATCH_MISALIGN &&     1938-1944
  |reg_pc[1:0] != 0 without COMPRESSED_ISA          resetn &&
                                                   mem_do_rinst
```

Five obligations.

1. **The data check reads `reg_op1`, not the presented address.** By the time a
   request flag is set, `reg_op1` holds the effective address
   ([[FSM-STMEM-001]]#1), and `mem_addr` has been word-aligned by `mem_la_addr`
   ([[MIF-LA-001]]) — so checking the bus address would find every access
   aligned.
2. **The data check is on `mem_wordsize`, and a byte access is never
   misaligned.** There are only two arms, for word and halfword; `mem_wordsize`
   2 has none ([[MEM-SIZE-001]]).
3. **The instruction check narrows under `COMPRESSED_ISA`** to `reg_pc[0]`
   alone, because a 16-bit instruction may start at any even address
   ([[RVC-001]]).
4. **The instruction check fires on `mem_do_rinst` and not on
   `mem_do_prefetch`**, so a prefetch to a misaligned address raises nothing —
   it cannot, because a prefetch's address is `reg_next_pc` advanced by 2 or 4
   from an address already checked ([[PC-ADV-001]]). An implementation that
   checks the prefetch traps on a target it was never going to execute.
5. **The data checks do NOT redirect.** Unlike the instruction cases of
   [[TRAP-ILL-001]], the escalating arms here set `next_irq_pending` and leave
   `cpu_state` alone (`picorv32.v:1925-1927`, `:1932-1934`) — so the misaligned
   access **proceeds** and the interrupt is taken when the instruction finishes.
   Only the halting arm assigns `cpu_state`. That asymmetry is in the RTL and an
   implementation that redirects here would skip the access.

With `CATCH_MISALIGN` off, neither check exists and the low address bits are
**forced to zero** on `reg_pc` and `reg_next_pc` every cycle instead
(`picorv32.v:1965-1972`, [[PC-ADV-001]]). A misaligned **data** access is then
not truncated at all — `reg_op1` is untouched — so the access proceeds with the
low bits as the byte-lane selector they already were
([[MEM-SIZE-001]]), and a word load from an odd address returns the word
containing it. That is silently wrong rather than detected, which is what
[[PRM-CATCH-001]] records.

**WHERE THE HALT IS REPORTED, MEASURED.** The instruction check fires in the cycle
*after* `reg_pc` becomes the misaligned address, because `reg_pc` is assigned
non-blockingly in `cpu_state_fetch` while `mem_do_rinst` rises with it
(`picorv32.v:1938`). By then no instruction at the new address has been decoded, so
`dbg_insn_addr` still holds the **previous** one — and the trap is therefore
reported as that instruction's retirement, carrying whatever register write it
performed (`picorv32.v:2014-2023`, [[VER-RVFI-001]]). There is **one** event, not
two: the retirement and the halt coincide.

That was established by running the module rather than by reading it
([[D-0004]]#1). `gen/tests/rtl.py` compiles `picorv32.v` with Verilator, runs it on
the same images the model runs, and compares its RVFI stream against
`gen/harness/refmodel.py`; the model and the reference both emitted two events
until 2026-09-09, and no real run produces that.

The data checks differ, and the difference is obligation 5's: the access is already
requested when the check fires, so the halt is reported on the instruction that
made it, at its own address.

nodes.label: Three conditions, each with two outcomes

definitionAnnotations.name: body
definitionAnnotations.text:
Exactly three conditions MUST be able to reach `cpu_state_trap`, and each MUST
prefer raising an **interrupt** over halting when three things hold: interrupts
are enabled, the corresponding mask bit is clear, and no interrupt routine is
already running.

```text ndf:normative
condition                       internal     raises     halts instead when
                                interrupt    clause
an undecoded instruction        1 (ebreak)   TRAP-      !ENABLE_IRQ, or
  (DEF-INSTRTRAP-001), an                    ILL-001    irq_mask[1], or
  ECALL, or an EBREAK                                   irq_active
a misaligned data access        2 (buserror) TRAP-      the same, with bit 2
                                             ALIGN-001
a misaligned instruction fetch  2 (buserror) TRAP-      the same
                                             ALIGN-001
```

The escalation test is written out identically in **six** places — three for
interrupt 1 and three for interrupt 2 (`picorv32.v:1608`, `:1619`, `:1780`,
`:1925`, `:1932`, `:1940`):

```text ndf:normative
if (ENABLE_IRQ && !irq_mask[irq_N] && !irq_active)
    next_irq_pending[irq_N] = 1;     -- a BLOCKING assignment
    and, for the instruction cases, cpu_state <= cpu_state_fetch
else
    cpu_state <= cpu_state_trap;
```

Three obligations.

1. **`irq_mask` resets to all ones** ([[ARCH-RESET-001]], [[IRQ-MASK-001]]), so
   **a core that has not executed `maskirq` halts** on any of the three. The
   README says so: "an illegal instruction or bus error while the illegal
   instruction or bus error interrupt is disabled will cause the processor to
   halt."
2. **`irq_active` blocks the escalation**, so a fault *inside* the interrupt
   routine halts rather than re-entering it. There is no nesting and no double
   fault ([[IRQ-ACTIVE-001]]).
3. **`MASKED_IRQ` can make the halt unconditional.** A bit set in that parameter
   is OR-ed into every `maskirq` write (`picorv32.v:1682`), so software cannot
   clear it and the condition halts for ever
   ([[PRM-IRQMASKS-001]], [[CON-BASIC-001]]#11).

---

definitionAnnotations.name: body
definitionAnnotations.text:
An undecoded instruction, an `ECALL` and an `EBREAK` MUST reach the **same**
escalation, and MUST reach it through the co-processor interface
([[PCPI-001]], [[DEC-TRAP-001]]):

```text ndf:normative
step                                                              line
1  instr_trap fires -- the NOR of 48 of the 49 decode flags,       679-685
   gated by CATCH_ILLINSN || WITH_PCPI. An ECALL sets it too,
   because instr_ecall_ebreak is the flag left OUT of the NOR
2  cpu_state_ld_rs1's first arm offers the instruction: pcpi_valid  1585-1625
   rises with pcpi_insn, pcpi_rs1 and pcpi_rs2 (PCPI-001).
   At one read port the offer is made in ld_rs2 instead            1768-1786
3  if pcpi_int_ready: take the result, drop pcpi_valid, go to       1598-1603
   cpu_state_fetch -- NOT a trap at all
4  else if CATCH_ILLINSN && (pcpi_timeout || instr_ecall_ebreak):   1605-1613
   escalate per TRAP-CAUSE-001 on interrupt 1
```

Four obligations.

1. **`instr_ecall_ebreak` short-circuits the timeout.** Step 4's disjunction
   means a system instruction escalates in the **first** cycle of
   `cpu_state_ld_rs1`, while an unknown instruction waits for `pcpi_timeout`
   ([[PCPI-TIMEOUT-001]]). So `ECALL` costs four cycles and an unclaimed
   instruction costs twenty ([[PIPE-CPI-001]]). The offer of step 2 is never
   SEEN for a system instruction: the escalation's `pcpi_valid <= 0` overrides
   the offer's `<= 1` in that same cycle ([[DEC-TRAP-001]]#3, measured
   2026-09-24).
2. **The escalation raises interrupt 1, not a cause code.** `irq_ebreak` is the
   localparam `1` ([[CON-WIDTH-001]]), and the interrupt routine learns which of
   the three conditions fired only from the **bitmask** in `q1`
   ([[IRQ-ENTRY-001]]) — which cannot distinguish an illegal instruction from an
   `ECALL` at all. That is a real loss of information relative to `mcause` and it
   is the machine's ([[D-0002]]).
3. **With `WITH_PCPI` and no `CATCH_ILLINSN`, the path HANGS.** Step 1 still
   fires, step 2 still offers, and step 4 is `CATCH_ILLINSN`-guarded — so
   nothing escalates and nothing advances. `pcpi_timeout_counter` is not even
   counted, its own guard being `WITH_PCPI && CATCH_ILLINSN`
   (`picorv32.v:1423`). The core stays in `cpu_state_ld_rs1` with `pcpi_valid`
   asserted and `trap` **low**, which is the one failure a testbench watching
   `trap` cannot see. MEASURED, 2026-09-09: at `CATCH_ILLINSN = 0` with
   `ENABLE_MUL` the machine retires the instructions before the undecoded one,
   emits no trapped event and reaches the harness's cycle bound
   ([[Q-003]], `gen/tests/questions.py`). Recorded also as
   [[CON-BASIC-001]]#12, which is why `gen/params.py` refuses to elaborate the
   combination at all.
4. **With neither `CATCH_ILLINSN` nor `WITH_PCPI`, `instr_trap` is constant
   zero** and an undecoded instruction is **executed** — it falls to
   `cpu_state_ld_rs1`'s default arm, reaches `cpu_state_exec`, and writes X to
   its destination register ([[DEC-TRAP-001]], [[ALU-OUT-001]]). It does not
   trap, interrupt or hang.

`ECALL` and `EBREAK` have a **second** path that exists only at
`!CATCH_ILLINSN` (`picorv32.v:1945-1947`):

```text ndf:normative
if (!CATCH_ILLINSN && decoder_trigger_q && !decoder_pseudo_trigger_q
    && instr_ecall_ebreak)
    cpu_state <= cpu_state_trap;
```

This is an **unconditional halt**: it does not consult `irq_mask` and does not
raise an interrupt, which is what the README means by "with this option set to
0, an `EBREAK` will trap the processor without triggering an interrupt". It sits
after the state `case` ([[FSM-POST-001]]) and therefore overrides whatever state
the `case` chose.

Its guard uses `decoder_trigger_q` and `decoder_pseudo_trigger_q` — the
**delayed** copies (`picorv32.v:1447`, `:1449`) — rather than the live signals,
because `instr_ecall_ebreak` is a phase-2 result and is not valid until the cycle
after `decoder_trigger` ([[DEC-PHASE-001]]). An implementation that tests the
live signals misses the halt by one cycle and then traps on the *following*
instruction.

definitionAnnotations.name: body
definitionAnnotations.text: TRAP-ALIGN-001: the instruction about to launch is misaligned: ONE event, the previous instruction's, marked trapped; then halt.

definitionAnnotations.name: body
definitionAnnotations.text: PCPI-001 step 4: the offer expired; escalate to the trap.

definitionAnnotations.name: body
definitionAnnotations.text: TRAP-ALIGN-001: the access is ISSUED (the RTL's check is after the case) and the machine halts.

definitionAnnotations.name: body
definitionAnnotations.text: FSM-LDRS1-001 arm 9: the conversion is issued BEFORE the load (MEM-PREFETCH-001#2's invariant); the address and its alignment here.

definitionAnnotations.name: body
definitionAnnotations.text: PCPI-001 step 2: an undecoded instruction is offered, to every core (MD-MUX-001#1's broadcast is one port a core), with the WORD.

definitionAnnotations.name: body
definitionAnnotations.text: FSM-LDRS1-001 arm 12. The effective address (FSM-STMEM-001#1) and its alignment are computed HERE, so the stmem guard reads one bit.

definitionAnnotations.name: body
definitionAnnotations.text: FSM-LDRS1-001 arm 1: straight to the trap -- no co-processor, or an ECALL/EBREAK, which the RTL escalates in the first ld_rs1 cycle (picorv32.v:1605) before any offer is seen.

definitionAnnotations.name: body
definitionAnnotations.text: TRAP-001: absorbing; one event says it happened.

nodes.label: The eight CPU states and their transitions

definitionAnnotations.name: body
definitionAnnotations.text:
The core MUST implement a state register `cpu_state` holding exactly these
eight states, **one-hot in eight bits** (`picorv32.v:1172-1181`):

```text ndf:normative
state               encoding    what occupies it
cpu_state_trap      8'b10000000 the machine has stopped (TRAP-001)
cpu_state_fetch     8'b01000000 retire the previous instruction, advance the
                                PC, launch the next (FSM-FETCH-001)
cpu_state_ld_rs1    8'b00100000 read the first source, and DISPATCH on the
                                decoded instruction (FSM-LDRS1-001)
cpu_state_ld_rs2    8'b00010000 read the second source, single-port register
                                file only (FSM-LDRS2-001)
cpu_state_exec      8'b00001000 take the ALU result, resolve control flow
                                (FSM-EXEC-001)
cpu_state_shift     8'b00000100 one iteration of a multi-cycle shift
                                (FSM-SHIFT-001)
cpu_state_stmem     8'b00000010 issue and complete a store (FSM-STMEM-001)
cpu_state_ldmem     8'b00000001 issue and complete a load (FSM-LDMEM-001)
```

The one-hot encoding is **not** an implementation detail to be optimized away:
`dbg_ascii_state` and the formal validity check both compare `cpu_state`
against the whole eight-bit constant (`picorv32.v:2126-2134`), and a
three-bit-index implementation would permit a ninth value the formal property
exists to exclude ([[VER-ASSERT-001]]).

The core MUST reset to `cpu_state_fetch` ([[ARCH-RESET-001]]) and MUST then
make exactly these transitions:

```text ndf:normative
from        to          when                                       line
(reset)     fetch       always                                     1483
fetch       fetch       no fresh decode yet; or an interrupt entry
                        pass; or `waitirq`; or a `jal`, whose
                        target needs no operand                    1491-1577
fetch       ld_rs1      a fresh decode, and the instruction is
                        not a `jal`                                1572-1575
ld_rs1      ld_rs1      an undecoded instruction is being offered
                        to the co-processor and it is not ready    1585-1625
ld_rs1      ld_rs2      the register file is single-port           1754
ld_rs1      exec        LUI / AUIPC / JAL link, JALR, an
                        immediate ALU form, or a shift with
                        BARREL_SHIFTER                             1641-1723
ld_rs1      shift       a shift-immediate without BARREL_SHIFTER   1704-1711
ld_rs1      stmem       a store, dual-port                         1737-1740
ld_rs1      ldmem       a load                                     1696-1703
ld_rs1      fetch       a counter read, a q-register instruction,
                        `retirq`, `maskirq`, `timer`, or a
                        co-processor result                        1626-1695
ld_rs1      trap        an undecoded instruction with nothing to
                        claim it and no interrupt to take          1585-1624
ld_rs2      ld_rs2      as ld_rs1 -> ld_rs1                        1768-1786
ld_rs2      stmem       a store                                    1787-1790
ld_rs2      shift       a register shift without BARREL_SHIFTER    1791-1793
ld_rs2      exec        anything else                              1794-1801
ld_rs2      fetch       a co-processor result                      1768-1786
ld_rs2      trap        as ld_rs1 -> trap                          1768-1786
exec        exec        TWO_CYCLE_ALU or TWO_CYCLE_COMPARE is
                        waiting (1807-1810); or a taken branch
                        whose re-fetch has not completed           1811-1820
exec        fetch       otherwise                                  1805-1827
shift       shift       the shift count has not reached zero       1835-1851
shift       fetch       the shift count has reached zero           1831-1834
stmem       stmem       the transfer has not completed             1854-1878
stmem       fetch       the transfer has completed                 1872-1876
ldmem       ldmem       the transfer has not completed             1880-1926
ldmem       fetch       the transfer has completed                 1900-1910
trap        trap        always -- the state is ABSORBING           1487-1489
```

Three properties of that table are normative and are easy to lose:

1. **`cpu_state_ld_rs1` reaches all eight states**, itself included. It is the
   machine's dispatch point: the decoded instruction selects the state, and the
   selection is a `case (1'b1)` over fourteen arms in a fixed order
   ([[FSM-LDRS1-001]]). No other state has more than three successors.
2. **`cpu_state_fetch` is reachable from every state and `cpu_state_trap` is
   reachable from all but one.** Every instruction ends by returning to
   `fetch`, which is what makes `fetch` and not a separate writeback stage the
   place the architectural write happens ([[REG-WRITE-001]]).
3. **A transition into `cpu_state_trap` MAY come from outside the table.**
   Three blocking assignments after the `case` statement override whatever the
   occupied state decided: a misaligned data access (`picorv32.v:1922-1937`), a
   misaligned instruction fetch (`:1938-1944`), and an `ECALL`/`EBREAK` when
   `CATCH_ILLINSN` is off (`:1945-1947`). They are specified by
   [[TRAP-ALIGN-001]] and [[TRAP-ILL-001]] and they MUST take precedence,
   because a blocking assignment in the same `always` block is what the RTL
   uses to express exactly that.

⟨COMB: `ld_rs1`'s dispatch reads the `instr_*` and `is_*` flags, `cpuregs_rs1`
and `cpuregs_rs2` in the same cycle it assigns `cpu_state`; the register file
read is combinational from `decoded_rs1` ([[REG-READ-001]])⟩

definitionAnnotations.name: body
definitionAnnotations.text:
Both default 1. They select whether the two trap-detection mechanisms exist at
all, and **switching one off does not make the condition harmless** — it makes
it undetected, which is the distinction an implementation MUST preserve.

```text ndf:normative
parameter       at 1                           at 0
CATCH_MISALIGN  a misaligned data access or    no check. The low address bits
                instruction fetch raises       are FORCED to zero instead, on
                IRQ 2 or halts                 reg_pc and reg_next_pc
                (TRAP-ALIGN-001)               (picorv32.v:1962-1969), and a
                                               misaligned DATA access simply
                                               uses the truncated address
CATCH_ILLINSN   an undecoded instruction, an   no illegal-instruction check
                ECALL or an EBREAK raises      and no co-processor timeout.
                IRQ 1 or halts after the       An ECALL or EBREAK still HALTS,
                co-processor timeout           unconditionally and without
                (TRAP-ILL-001)                 raising an interrupt
                                               (picorv32.v:1945-1947)
```

`CATCH_ILLINSN` at 0 is the subtler of the two and the README says so: an
`EBREAK` still traps, it simply stops raising IRQ 1 first. The mechanism is a
separate `if` after the state `case`, reached only when `!CATCH_ILLINSN`
([[PIPE-FSM-001]]), so the two paths to `cpu_state_trap` are different code and
only one of them can ever be present.

`instr_trap` itself is `(CATCH_ILLINSN || WITH_PCPI) && !{…}`
(`picorv32.v:679`), so an undecoded instruction is still **detected** when
`CATCH_ILLINSN` is 0 as long as some co-processor is present — it is offered to
the interface and, if unclaimed, the core hangs in `cpu_state_ld_rs1` with
`pcpi_valid` asserted, because the timeout that would have rescued it is
`CATCH_ILLINSN`-guarded (`picorv32.v:1605`, `:1777`). Recorded as an obligation of
[[TRAP-ILL-001]] and tracked by [[Q-003]].

---

nodes.label: Q-003: an undecoded instruction hangs when `CATCH_ILLINSN` is off and a co-processor is present

definitionAnnotations.name: body
definitionAnnotations.text:
`instr_trap` — the NOR of the whole decoded instruction set
([[DEF-INSTRTRAP-001]]) — is gated on `CATCH_ILLINSN || WITH_PCPI`
(`picorv32.v:679`). The sixteen-cycle timeout that rescues an instruction no
co-processor claims is gated on `CATCH_ILLINSN` alone
(`picorv32.v:1605`, `:1777`).

So at `CATCH_ILLINSN = 0` with any of `ENABLE_PCPI`, `ENABLE_MUL`,
`ENABLE_FAST_MUL` or `ENABLE_DIV` set:

1. An undecoded instruction still sets `instr_trap`, because `WITH_PCPI` is
   true.
2. `cpu_state_ld_rs1` still raises `pcpi_valid` and offers it
   (`picorv32.v:1586-1624`).
3. If nothing asserts `pcpi_ready` — which is every instruction the attached
   core does not implement — there is no timeout, no trap and no transition.
   The core **stays in `cpu_state_ld_rs1` with `pcpi_valid` asserted, for
   ever**.

`pcpi_timeout_counter` is still counted down, because its own guard is
`WITH_PCPI && CATCH_ILLINSN` (`picorv32.v:1423`) — so at
`CATCH_ILLINSN = 0` it is not counted at all, and `pcpi_timeout` is never set.
The machine does not trap, does not interrupt and does not halt: it hangs with
`trap` low, which is the one failure mode a testbench watching `trap` cannot
see.

**Tested, 2026-09-09:** read from the three guards named above rather than
simulated. What would settle it is `make test` with `-DCATCH_ILLINSN=0` and
`ENABLE_MUL=1` and a program containing one `DIV` — the multiplier core does
not claim it — which is the experiment this entry is asking for and which has
not been run. Recording the bound without the simulation is what [[D-0004]]
requires to be said out loud.

**Why it may be intended.** `CATCH_ILLINSN = 0` means "I have removed the
illegal-instruction circuitry", and the README is explicit that an `EBREAK`
still traps at that setting while no longer raising IRQ 1. A reading in which
the parameter also removes the timeout — so that a co-processor is trusted to
claim everything offered to it — is coherent, and in a closed system where the
integrator knows the instruction set it is free area.

**Why it may not be.** The combination is not documented, no named
configuration point uses it ([[CON-CFG-001]]), and the failure is silent. The
alternative implementation — keep the timeout whenever `WITH_PCPI`, and halt
rather than interrupt at `CATCH_ILLINSN = 0` — costs the same counter and has
no silent mode.

**The question.** Whether [[TRAP-ILL-001]] should state the hang as a
**property of the machine** at that parameter combination, or
[[CON-BASIC-001]] should state the combination as **excluded**. Row 12 of
[[CON-BASIC-001]] currently does the second, which has the effect of declaring
a parameter combination out of scope on this tree's authority rather than on
the RTL's — and this tree's authority does not extend to narrowing the design
space ([[D-0001]]).

The honest resolution is probably both: the constraint for a reader choosing
parameters, and the property for a reader implementing the machine. What is
undecided is whether the property is a defect to report upstream. The project
is archived, so there is nowhere to report it.

nodes.label: A trapped core is detected by `trap` and by nothing else

definitionAnnotations.name: body
definitionAnnotations.text:
A test MUST detect a halt by watching the `trap` output, and MUST NOT detect it by
waiting for activity to cease: a trapped core still counts cycles and still counts
its timer down ([[TRAP-001]]).

A test MUST additionally distinguish a halt from a **hang**, which `trap` does
not report. Two hangs are reachable and neither asserts it:

```text ndf:normative
hang                                                        clause
an unclaimed instruction at CATCH_ILLINSN = 0 with a        Q-003
co-processor present: ld_rs1 with pcpi_valid asserted and
no timeout
a memory peer that never asserts mem_ready                  MIF-001
```

So a test MUST carry a step or cycle bound of its own, and a run that reaches it
MUST be reported as a failure rather than as completion. `testbench.v` does this
with a `$finish` on a memory-mapped write and a cycle limit; the model does it
with the runtime's iteration bound.
